A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SemHiTok and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting comparison. All 11 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v4 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix. Changed experimental settings limit direct performance comparisons, but not comparison of the papers.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, multimodal understanding, text-to-image generation and ablation results in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v4 reports original tokenizer and unified-MLLM experiments, including reconstruction, understanding, generation and component ablations in Tables 2 and 4–9.

M1.justification: The hierarchical tokenizer remains, but v4 introduces a Dual-MLP adapter that separately projects semantic and pixel features, and develops one unified MLLM with a universal next-token objective instead of v1's separate downstream models. The reported semantic loss also gains an absolute-error term. Codebook flattening and EMA updates were already present in v1.

E1.justification: GenAI-Bench replaces GenEval, introducing basic and advanced compositional generation evaluation. Training coverage expands to language-only instruction corpora and MidJourney-style synthetic images, alongside retained COYO, ImageNet and understanding data. v4 Table 5 also adds an MMV-labelled evaluation column, although the PDF does not define that benchmark.

E2.justification: Reconstruction comparisons add FQGAN, TokLIP and UniTok and remove VQGAN. Generation comparisons add Playgroundv2.5, ILLUME, Liquid and UniTok while removing SD v1.5, Transfusion, LlamaGen and EMU3. Understanding comparator membership is also substantially revised, including the dedicated tokenizer comparison with SigLIP in v4 Table 4.

E3.justification: v1 uses Vicuna-7B for understanding and Qwen2.5-3B for generation; v4 evaluates a jointly trained Qwen2.5-7B with a new mixed pretraining and instruction-tuning recipe. v4 adds a tokenizer comparison mostly sharing the Vicuna/LLaVA setting, 384-resolution reconstruction and generation evaluations, and GenAI-Bench VQA scoring. Its ablation design also specifies 40 ImageNet training epochs.

E4.justification: The key-component study is redesigned: the semantic-encoder initialization test disappears, while Dual-MLP and enhanced-decoder ablations are added in v4 Table 7. Table 9 adds semantic quantization-type and codebook-dimension analyses. Figures 6–7 add reconstruction-stage comparisons and understanding examples. The fusion/sub-codebook-size study is retained as Table 8, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both present experimental results as point estimates.

E6.justification: v1 reports reconstruction rFID 1.10 for ImageNet-only training and 1.24 after broader training; v4 reports 1.16 at 256 and 0.66 at 384. Generation reporting changes from GenEval 0.66 and MJHQ30K gFID 11.0 to new GenAI-Bench results and gFID 5.40 at 256, with different models and training. In the retained fusion study, usage changes from 98.4% to 95.4% without semantic features and from 97.1% to 94.1% for length concatenation.

T1.justification: The semantic-loss definition changes from cosine loss plus a quantization-loss description in v1 Section 3.1 to cosine plus absolute error in v4 Equation 3. The added EMA equation explains an update already specified in v1. Neither version provides new theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v4 makes an actual unified MLLM and compatibility with a shared text-image prediction head explicit contributions. Its headline generation claim shifts from superiority on GenEval to MJHQ30K state of the art among unified MLLMs, with stronger claims about approaching or surpassing continuous-input models. The central hierarchical-decoupling claim remains.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations for Dual-MLP feature separation, enhanced-decoder benefits and the suitability of EMA over normalized semantic quantization. It removes v1's limitations and future-work discussion concerning semantic-codebook exploration and higher resolutions, while partially addressing these experimentally. The central interpretations of SGHC and dimensional fusion remain.

D1.justification: v4 Table 3 newly supplies stage-specific learning rates and batch sizes; the text adds normalized pixel quantization, semantic dimension 48 and detailed unified-MLLM data mixtures. v1's lmms-eval and inference guidance-scale disclosures disappear. Reproducibility remains limited by conflicting v4 specifications: eight versus twelve default pixel sub-codes, and 50M versus 20M COYO for PRE fine-tuning.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning around structural separation, separate training and shared-head compatibility, including the new characteristics comparison in Table 1. It adds relevant work such as FQGAN, TokLIP, UniTok and Liquid, while removing references including GenEval, Transfusion and NExT-GPT. Much of the general related-work prose remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution framing, downstream-method discussion, experimental narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. SPC becomes the semantic codebook, and pixel terminology largely replaces texture terminology. Experiments are reorganized around tokenizer evaluation and a unified MLLM; the limitations and future-work paragraphs are removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one. Architecture diagrams are redrawn and combined with a codebook-flattening illustration in v4 Figure 3; new comparison, training and ablation tables and qualitative figures substantially restructure presentation. The generation gallery is replaced and enlarged, but loses v1's per-image prompts.

improvement.justification: The unified-model demonstration, more controlled tokenizer comparison and adapter/quantizer ablations strengthen evidence for the paper's central goal beyond v1's separate downstream demonstrations. Training disclosure also improves. However, conflicting sub-codebook and data-size specifications weaken reproducibility, and the reconstruction-SOTA claim conflicts with Table 2's UniTok rFID of 0.39 versus SemHiTok's 1.16 at 256. Together with removed limitations, these problems constrain the otherwise useful gains to a limited overall improvement.
